look_here_first: Start with life form and the underside of the flower. Tall poppymallow is an annual (sometimes biennial) with one to several erect/weakly erect stems and NO involucellar bractlets beneath the calyx. In bud the calyx lobes meet valvately to form a pointed tip.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: typically erect to weakly erect, often 40–95 cm in Williamson material

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: basal rosette early, often gone by flowering

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves alternate, palmately 3–7-lobed, becoming smaller/narrower upward

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: foliage somewhat velvety with simple and mostly 4-rayed stellate hairs

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx lobes valvate in bud, forming an apiculate/acuminate point

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: schizocarps smaller than winecup; 10–14 glabrous dehiscent mericarps with prominent beaks and 3-lobed collars

lookalikes.differences: Callirhoe involucrata: Winecup is perennial and low/trailing with 3 involucellar bractlets; C. leiocarpa is annual/tall and has no involucel. Callirhoe pedata: Older records can confuse these taxa. C. leiocarpa is annual with auriculate stipules and dehiscent mericarps; true C. pedata is perennial. Callirhoe scabriuscula: Texas poppy-mallow is a stiffly erect perennial with dense 6–8-rayed stellate hairs and an involucel; C. leiocarpa is annual and lacks the involucel.
